or (b) an employee; or (c) a person providing, or proposing to provide, services for the benefit of the Trade Marks Office."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s224","quote":"(2) If, because of: (a) an error or omission by the person concerned or by his or her agent; or (b) circumstances beyond the control of the person concerned; a relevant act that is required by this Act to be done within a certain time is not, or cannot be, done within that time, the Registrar may, on application made by the person concerned in accordance with the regulations, extend the time for doing the act."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s224","quote":"(3) If: (a) a relevant act that a person is required by this Act to do within a certain time is not, or cannot be, done within that time; and (b) on application made by that person in accordance with the regulations, the Registrar is of the opinion that special circumstances exist that justify an extension of that time; the Registrar may extend the time for doing the act."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s224","quote":"(4) The time allowed for doing a relevant act may be extended, whether before or after that time has expired."},{"ref":"TMR1995/r21.25","quote":"For the purposes of subsections 224(2) and (3) of the Act (which deal with extensions of time), an application for an extension of time for doing a relevant act: (a) must be in an approved form; and (b) must be accompanied by a declaration stating: (i) the facts on which the grounds specified in the application are based; and (ii) if the period for doing the relevant act has ended—the reason why the application was not made before the period ended."}],"answer":"The supplied passages do not give the specific test for extending an opposition evidence deadline. I cannot establish from them whether the general section 224 route applies to that deadline, so the following is conditional—not a complete evidence-extension checklist.

**Manual practice:** The Manual acknowledges applications for extensions of evidence periods and describes temporary suspension for settlement negotiations as an alternative to successive extensions. It does not set out the evidence-extension eligibility test in the supplied excerpt. [TMM/Part51/4/4/1~1]

**Act—general extension grounds, if section 224 applies:**
- Under section 224(2), show that an error or omission by you or your agent, or circumstances beyond your control, caused the relevant act not to be done—or to be unable to be done—in time. The Registrar may extend time. [TMA1995/s224]
- Under section 224(3), the Registrar must consider that special circumstances exist justifying an extension where the relevant act was not, or cannot be, done in time. The power to extend is discretionary. [TMA1995/s224]
- Section 224(1) requires an extension where the failure or inability to act in time results from an error or omission by the specified Office personnel or service providers. [TMA1995/s224]
- Section 224(4) permits an extension before or after the time has expired. [TMA1995/s224]

**Regulations—supporting material for a section 224(2) or (3) application:** Use the approved form and provide a declaration stating the facts supporting your grounds. If the deadline has passed, also explain why the extension application was not made before it expired. [TMR1995/r21.25]

The evidence-specific extension provisions are needed before this can be treated as definitive guidance for an opposition evidence deadline."}
